second_order: Repeating and policing the challenge-image gag
theme_note: A poster repeatedly issued the same FDev challenge image while commenters counted, laughed at, questioned, and failed to understand the repetition and moderators removed duplicates and threatened a ban. What varies is response: amusement, confusion, spam complaint, or formal containment.

second_order: Turning the subreddit into No Man's Elite
theme_note: Participants enacted and interpreted the room's No Man's Sky makeover by changing its frame, relabelling game material, visiting the paired subreddit, playing along, and eventually naming or exposing the April Fools device. Posts perform the crossover; comments vary between extension, praise, confusion, comparison, and disclosure.

second_order: Finding a drawable Elite mark and somewhere to put it
theme_note: Participants moved from calls to draw toward candidate words or ships, coordinates, and available space, then regrouped when an attempted patch was overwritten or contested. The target varies from ELITE or DANGEROUS to an Asp, Cobra, or Sidewinder, and no early proposal is treated as a durable result.

second_order: Keeping straight-faced Elite April Fools stories going
theme_note: Posters launched fake Elite offers, updates, announcements, organizations, and old-or-other-game reveals; replies sustained, embellished, challenged, or exposed those fictions. The story changes, but the shared practice is collaboratively maintaining or puncturing a plausible-sounding Elite claim rather than changing the subreddit style itself.

second_order: Funnelling duplicate r/place posts into active threads
theme_note: Moderators treated repeated canvas proposals, images, and alarms as duplicates and sent them back to already active discussions; authors sometimes apologized or contested whether the event was really the same. What varies is the duplicated object and whether removal is accepted immediately.

second_order: Building and repairing the Elite mark one pixel at a time
theme_note: Participants chose the 675,252 site, requested a grid, contributed on the five-minute cycle, reported local completion, repaired damage, and recounted the labour. The state varies from forming to flawed, attacked, repaired, or briefly perfect, so completion is recurrent rather than a single permanent moment.

second_order: Trading space and protection with canvas neighbours
theme_note: Participants negotiated the New Zealand laser and surrounding claims, requested or offered help, exchanged pixel labour, adjusted borders, and later defended neighbouring space-game marks. What varies is the counterpart and the bargain: peace, relocation, a border repair, a reciprocal build, or mutual defence.

second_order: Proposing additions and side missions around the logo
theme_note: Participants proposed optional work beside or beyond the core Elite mark: another community logo, an invasion, a slogan, a ship, or a colour change. Replies test feasibility, purpose, and available pixels, and several proposals disappear without a demonstrated result.

second_order: Sounding alarms and checking threats to the territory
theme_note: Participants called others back when marks were attacked, asked commanders to stay vigilant, relayed or corrected threat intelligence, and disputed whether defence mattered. Reports vary from visible damage to rumours from hidden channels, and replies range from readiness to skepticism that it was only bots versus bots.

One deleted-body thread survives only as the title '[r/place]'. Its words establish posting the venue marker but not building, bargaining, warning, or any other recoverable practice, so it remains a single-code theme rather than being grouped by adjacency.

second_order: Carrying the logo into successor canvases
theme_note: After or around the canvas close, participants displayed or proposed rebuilding the communal mark on an r/place Minecraft recreation and pxls.space. What varies is whether the successor is commemorative or a fresh recruitment call; the Reddit record does not establish that the pxls.space calls produced a maintained image.

second_order: Celebrating and retelling how they left their mark
theme_note: Participants treated the locked canvas as a shared accomplishment, thanked pixel defenders, recounted correcting letters and helping neighbours, explained bots and alliances, and shared final frames. Their stories vary in whom they credit and which conflict they foreground, but they jointly turn repeated repair into a finished community memory.
